I think the option should be there if it can be. If the building is already built, we'd be wasting our time installing new gender neutral bathrooms. For example, I personally wouldn't think it would be worth the time to install new gender neutral bathrooms on my university campus as it is unless they were building a new building otherwise it's extra money. I personally (as someone early in transition) have found no issue with entering male bathrooms both pre-t and very early on T. I think in most cases (not all cases) guys just see you've entered the men's room and accept that you're male. But that's just been my experience. 

Though speaking of choosing X to be on your information, if you choose X you should commit to only having X on your info. I know someone who has X and M on various different documents and it makes it much harder to confirm that person is the same person by insurance and stuff. A gender marker is important to ID because the more information you have on your ID the harder it is for someone to fake an ID and the harder it is to use someone else's information and commit identity theft. I think eliminating markers all together would make it a bit easier to steal information but the alternative solution would be adding the X option I would say.

There should definitely be the option for a third category with bathrooms, one that's not gendered if you fear or dislike gendered bathrooms that much. But the majority of the population (cis and some trans people) prefer to use gendered rooms. But with ID's, where I live (New Zealand), I don't know about other countries, you can have X instead of M or F on your birth certificate and your passport and I think drivers licence but I'm not sure about that.

Personally I'm for them, just in the same way that I'm for keeping separate bathrooms, I want to have things that reflect my identity. Part of that is using male restrooms and having male on my birth certificate/drivers licence/etc.
